messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> service=autoscale-controller severity=critical incident=PD-12345 queue_depth=5421 waitlist_len=4100 kvcache_warmup=false

pagerduty: page auto-fired to Emma (oncall rotation) and escalation chain (raj.sre, kai.runtime). Open incident link: https://pd.redwood/PD-12345

Emma (oncall): Acked. I'm jumping in — collecting quick scope: what's impacted?

maria (pm): Customer telemetry shows increased 429s for hosted-generation routes, mostly small-token calls. ~5% error rate globally; p95 latency ~1.2s up from 380ms. A subset of customers on shared pool seeing waitlist responses.

raj (sre): Thanks. Looks like autoscaler isn't keeping up with a sudden burst. Metrics: node-provision-time spiked to 90s, kube-scheduler backlog, spot instances slower. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but failed due to quota/spot delays.

kai (runtime): Noting KV prefix cache warmup is disabled for new nodes and warmup traffic is causing heavy cold-prefix loads. Prefix heat map shows many new keys. Queue backlog is tripping the request router's waitlist gate.

Emma (oncall): Can someone paste the K8s pod state?

kai (runtime): 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-worker-56d7f7f4b-abcde        0/1     Pending   0          3m
inference-worker-56d7f7f4b-bcdef        1/1     Running   0          18m
inference-worker-56d7f7f4b-cdef0        0/1     Pending   0          2m
inference-worker-56d7f7f4b-def01        0/1     ContainerCreating 0   1m
node/autoscale-node-172                 NotReady  0h
```

kai (runtime): Lots of Pending pods, Image pull fine, nodes stuck provisioning (cloud provider).

devops-bot: GCE API rate limit observed on provider logs for project redwood-prod: quotaExceeded on instance insert.

raj (sre): That explains it — autoscaler requested nodes but provider throttled. We'll need to either use reserved capacity or reroute traffic to fallback pools.

Emma (oncall): Tactical plan: 1) Force-scale a warm standby pool (reserved) for high-priority customers; 2) Update routing policy to move non-SLAd customers to fallback-llm; 3) Kick an ops-run to check quota and request emergency increase.

kai (runtime): I can flip routing rule for non-SLA IDs to model:open-medium-fallback with lower capacity. Small command to flip: 
```
PATCH /routing/policies/active
{ "rule": "if tenant.sla != 'enterprise' => route: open-medium-fallback" }
```
I'll stage a canary at 10% first.

maria (pm): Do it. Prioritize customers with payments flagged as enterprise. Notify support.

Emma (oncall): Executing emergency actions now. Manually invoked API to spin reserved pool: 
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/pools/force_start -d '{"pool":"reserved-warm-1","count":12,"reason":"PD-12345 emergency"}'
```
Response: 202 Accepted, request id req-9b3f. Nodes starting.

pagerduty: PD-12345 acknowledged by Emma (oncall). Escalation to raj.sre in 8m if no progress.

raj (sre): I'm on quota call with cloud provider. If they can't lift, we should fallback more aggressively and consider enabling preemptible fallback to keep request throughput. Also will check reserved pool billing tags.

kai (runtime): Routing canary at 10% done. Early signs: waitlist depth down 8% on canary shards, errors for canary users decreased. Rolling to 50% now.

Emma (oncall): Observability: p95 latency trending down to 820ms overall after canary routing. Error rate dropping to 3.1% from 5%. Good sign.

devops-bot: Cloud quota increase request submitted (ticket 98765) — provider estimated ETA 20-40 minutes.

maria (pm): Support message draft ready — short note that we've identified capacity cold-start issue, mitigation in progress, prioritized customers first. I'll send to customer comms channel in 10m.

raj (sre): While we wait on provider, let's enable aggressive pod warmup for new nodes (preload common KV prefixes). Kai — can you deploy warmup job?

kai (runtime): Deploying warmup job now. Snippet: 
```
kubectl apply -f jobs/kv-warmup.yaml --namespace=inference
```
Warmup job will run with batch size 200k prefixes across shards.

Emma (oncall): Update: reserved-warm-1 pool shows nodes becoming Ready. Pod Pending count decreasing.

kai (runtime): Confirm: new nodes are up and joining, but KV cache needs ~60s to warm per node — expect full recovery in ~6-8 minutes post-warmup.

Emma (oncall): Paging cadence: I'm staying on thread until we stabilize p95 < 700ms and waitlist_len < 300. After that I'll hand to Raj for root cause and follow-up.

pagerduty: PD-12345 status changed -> acknowledged by Emma (oncall).

raj (sre): I'll take postmortem and follow up about quota-proofing autoscaler and potential reserved pool sizing. Emma — thanks for triage. Handing incident to me for RCA.

Emma (oncall): Handoff complete. Last update: p95 680ms, error rate 1.9%, waitlist_len 280. Moving to monitoring-only. If anything regresses, ping me or escalate to PD.

maria (pm): Sending comms to affected customers now. cc @support.

devops-bot: Incident PD-12345 closed (auto) after successful mitigation window. Please file RCA with timeline within 48h.

Emma (oncall): Filing immediate notes in /incidents/PD-12345 and tagging Raj for RCA.

raj (sre): Received. Will include follow-ups: quota limits, autoscaler backoff tuning, warmup automation, and routing fallback thresholds.

kai (runtime): Adding runbook update PR for enabling fast warmup on node join.

Emma (oncall): Thanks team. Off-rotation in 25m.

maria (pm): Great work.
